sections.text: Indifference, non-attachment to sex, progeny or home, equanimity in good fortune and in bad;
Unswerving devotion to Me, by concentration on Me and Me alone, a love for solitude, indifference to social life;
Constant yearning for the knowledge of Self, and pondering over the lessons of the great Truth - this is Wisdom, all else ignorance.

We have been discussing chapter 13. First we saw the definition of the Kshetra. The Kshetra is defined as everything that I can see, perceive, and think -- that is my field.
The knower is the next subject of discussion. In the last few verses, we have been seeing the qualities of a seeker who wants to know. These qualities need to develop, or will develop, in the seeker because of his Mumukshutva, his desire to liberate himself from this limitation.
All the qualities we are seeing are attributes which become the cause for that revelation. The last quality we saw was Putra-dara-griha-adishu. One should be non-attached, not identifying with the putra, dara, griha, and so on.
That which we commonly consider as something I need to be attached to, something I need to be identified with -- here Bhagavan says you should not be identified with it. Nityam cha sama-chittatvam ishta-anishta-upapattishu -- one becomes equanimous in all situations, whether ishta or anishta, whether conducive or non-conducive. In other words, we have been given a pointer: because we have defined the Kshetra as that which I can perceive, and the Kshetrajna as that which is not the field but the knower.
Right now, my identification with my family and my possessions creates this notion that they are part of me. Therefore, the prescription here is: you need to develop non-identification. It did not say do not have a relationship with them. They are my relationships.
Putra, dara, griha -- all these are my relationships, my possessions, my acquisitions, my achievements. All these I should see as something other than me. With my identification remaining with the self, I can now relate to them.
That right relationship forms the right sort of dharma for the relationship. I follow that dharma without identifying myself with it -- that is basically the prescription. And therefore it will remain the same all the time, because you realize these are my relationships, and relationships are constantly changing.
No matter what the situation is, I remain constant in my identification and see the relationship developing and changing. Sometimes the situation may be ishta -- something which I think is conducive to me. And sometimes it is not.
When children come to us, we consider that as ishta. But when they want to move away from you, we dont consider that ishta. But knowing that it is for their own good, we feel good about letting them go.
If I have not understood the concept that I need to let the children go for their own good, I will be in the path of their progress. That close identification may cause a person not to achieve his or her full potential. So non-identification is very necessary.
Bhagavan says, whether the condition is ishta or anishta, conducive or non-conducive, remain equanimous. Then we continued into a few more qualities which Bhagavan says are very essential to understand the nature of the knower. Who is it that is perceiving? Me is this mind and intellect, and then the ego it creates.
The prescription here is given because, if I have developed the other qualities we discussed, then you have conserved lots of energy -- mental energy, intellectual energy. Now you have to apply that somewhere, so that it has its own field of action. So the next verse is: Mayi cha ananya-yogena, bhaktih avyabhicharini.
I take all this identification I have right now in this world -- which grounds my personality, grounds my self-esteem, grounds my identity about who I am. You take all this away from me, and I forget Im an architect. I forget I have a house, and Im nothing.
My grounding in this world is because of my identification with my family, my friends, my organizations, my accomplishments, my profession. Now, up till now you heard that -- take all that away from you. Where can all that energy which I had been putting into identification go? Bhagavan says: Mayi cha, ananya-yogena.
You now shift all that identification to Me. There, I have an identification. Here, I have a relationship.
Previously I thought my identification is my relationship, and my relationship is my identification. Because I identify, I have a relationship. Take the identification part and assign it to Me.
Just leave the relationship. So Ananya means none other. Identification with none other -- and then relating to the world as the field of your activity, the field of your actions, the field of performing your duties. Bhagavan says this will relieve you from that burden.
Bhaktih avyabhicharini -- devotion, love for the divine. We talked about taking this identification. And assigning to the one supreme entity.
Who I consider my own self. Which is other than this body, this mind, this intellect. Everything that I know right now is not that.
Move all that identification to that. And it should be Ananya -- no other identification lingers around. Somebody says, Are you faithful to your wife? Im very faithful, except that I have a couple of love affairs. Is he really faithful? The very fact that you have other affairs means you are not faithful.
But people do convince themselves that they are faithful because they are taking care of things. Bhagavan said that kind of identification with Me will not be very helpful. Therefore, bhakti avyabhicharini. Vyabhichari, in our normal context, refers to someone doing something which is disloyal to his own relationship or his own duties.
We do that to gain something frivolous. We perform that act for a momentary pleasure -- no real relationship, but just to get some pleasure for the time being. That is called vyabhichara.
We can relate that to our identification with the Supreme. Are you devoted to Bhagavan? I am very devoted to God. However, this is very important to me. This relationship is very important.
Well, first is my wife and then my Bhagavan. Your bhakti should be avyabhicharini -- for no small gain will you shift your identification even for a moment to something other than Me. Youll be constantly identified with Me, and then functioning in this world. We have seen s standard example of an actor performing his part on the stage.
Hes never truly identified with the role. Hes truly identified with himself, knowing fully who he is. Hes performing his role very effectively -- thats the only reason he can perform his role effectively.
Because he knows he is not the beggar that he is playing; he has a house in Beverly Hills. Therefore he can act the beggar so effectively. If he forgets he is an actor who is a multimillionaire, he will not be able to perform that act.
So Bhagavan said you will be more effective in your relationships. Your bhakti with Me should be avyabhicharini -- never leaving that for small, petty gains. We identify with things for our small pleasure, small gain in this world, and Bhagavan said thats what prevents you from realizing yourself.
Mayi cha ananya-yogena. This is like a new word coined by Krishna in Bhagavad Gita: Ananya Yoga. Nowhere in the earlier scriptures does the word Ananya Yoga appear.
But Krishna, in rejuvenating this whole knowledge, is coining new words. Ananya Yoga -- union with none other. My union with Him is so firm that there is no other identification.
Vivikta-desha-sevitvam. So now, if I am the only one in this room, am I by myself? Am I in solitude or in company? Well, of course, Rajan, youre in solitude because theres nobody else here. He said, vivikta-desha-sevitvam.
I should be practicing to be in solitude, not loneliness. You dont want to be lonely -- you want to be in solitude. So everybody said, Well, that means what I had been thinking all along -- this is not going to work.
I want to work my profession, have family, friends, all that, and then Im trying to understand Bhagavad Gita. Bhagavad Gita itself says go into solitude, then only you will know. Bhagavan said, not really. Solitude is when I identify with that Self that alone exists.
Then nothing exists other than that. I am never really in anothers company. Everything else is nothing but my own manifestation.
Everything else is nothing but my own Leela. Then obviously Im in complete solitude. When Im here by myself, everything I do is just me.
I say something, I hear that. But its solitude because its all me. Thats why I said, in Surat when I was growing up, there was a Maun Mandir for a saint.
In the Maun Mandir, you dont even have to take Bhagavans name when you go there. You just go into that room -- Maun Mandir, they called it -- and do whatever you want. You can take the books of your profession and read them.
You can take a radio or you can take anything -- there are no conditions. But you can take books, any type of books, and you can read there. The point is, you are by yourself.
Whatever I do is echoing my own thoughts, echoing my own self. Im in complete solitude because Im identifying with nothing other than me alone. That sense of being, establishing yourself in it, creates this solitude.
The world is going around me, but its like a dream, and therefore Im in complete solitude. Vivikta-desha-sevitvam, aratih janasamsadi -- and he develops a distaste for the company of other people. Obviously, once Im identified with Him, I see everything else is just a temporary relationship.
So I will not be craving for their company; Ill be craving to be in my own Self. I may have relationships and therefore duties to perform. I get together with them, I talk to them, but Im always in my solitude.
Im not craving for their company because my identification is gone. What do we really crave for? We identify with someone and say, I really need to go and see my mom, or I need to go and see such and such, only because we have an identification. Once the identification is shifted from this field to the knower of the field, obviously there is no craving for this field.
So Bhagavan continues. Now he says, what is the purpose of all these things? Adhyatma-jnana-nityatvam, Tattva-jnana-artha-darshanam. For the purpose of knowing the Tattva, that knowledge which I am seeking.
As we say, my true nature is Sat, Chit, and Ananda. The Chit is seeking the knowledge. But right now it is gaining knowledge which is actually in my way.
To know my true knowledge, I need to do all that which is prescribed in these few verses. Now I will build a Tattva-jnana-artha-darshanam. I can see the light at the end of the tunnel.
I can see what my goal is. Ed that even when we go to the station and ask, Which is the train to Madras? -- thats because the train is not in Madras right now, but it is going to Madras. So right now I may not be there, but I see the goal for my being, where my identification will be established.
Thats why Tattva-jnana-artha-darshanam -- I will know the essence of the knowledge about me. Adhyatma-jnana-nityatvam -- constancy of Self-knowledge. See, in our case we get a glimpse of who I am, but then we constantly shift and identify with something else which is also temporary.
At no time do we have a constancy of identification about who I am, what I am. At some point I thought Im a very good student. At some point I thought, well, Im a very good worker.
My identification keeps shifting to different roles and accomplishments, never constant.

These verses complete the enumeration of knowledge with profound instructions: non-attachment to family and possessions (asakti), equanimity in favorable and unfavorable circumstances (sama-chittatvam), unswerving devotion to the Lord (ananya-yoga bhakti), love of solitude (vivikta-desha-sevitvam), and constant pursuit of Self-knowledge (adhyatma-jnana-nityatvam). The key teaching here is the difference between relationship and identification. Krishna does not ask you to abandon your family (putra, dara, griha) but to stop identifying with them. Your spouse, children, and home are relationships to be honored through dharma - but your sense of self should not depend on them.
The concept of ananya-yoga - union with none other - is revolutionary. Right now, your identity is scattered across many identifications: profession, family, achievements, possessions. What if all that energy of identification were gathered and redirected toward the Supreme? This is not abandonment of worldly duties but a shift in where you anchor your sense of self. Reflect today: what would your life look like if you maintained all your relationships and responsibilities, but your fundamental identity rested in the unchanging Self rather than changing circumstances?
Verse 12 declares: This is knowledge; whatever is contrary to this is ignorance. As a practice, examine your mental and emotional reactions today. When you feel disturbed, ask: Which quality of knowledge am I forgetting right now? Am I attached when I should be witnessing? Am I craving company when I could rest in inner solitude? This discrimination between knowledge and ignorance is itself the path.
